evidence.field: 字形演變; specimen labels; commentary
evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone, bronze (including 集成02837), Chu manuscript, small-seal and Shuowen forms. Its commentary interprets the early graph as clothing with overlapping front lapels. The displayed sequence does not give specimen-level dates or a stroke-by-stroke account.
evidence.title: 漢字「衣」：字形演變

evidence.source: Chinese University of Hong Kong, Multi-function Chinese Character Database
evidence.field: 甲骨部件分析; 形義通解; reported inscription uses
evidence.text: The database describes oracle-bone and bronze 衣 as an upper garment, identifying collar, sleeves and overlapping lapels. It reports oracle-bone uses as place, personal and sacrificial names, and cites the bronze inscription 無叀鼎「易(賜)女(汝)玄衣」 for an upper-garment use. Its reports of graph use for 卒 and a 通讀 as 殷 concern particular disputed inscriptions and do not establish those senses as the word’s basic meaning.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫：漢字甲骨部件分析—衣

evidence.field: 衣 yī/yì; definitions and cited examples
evidence.text: The dictionary distinguishes noun yī ‘upper garment’ and ‘clothing generally’ from verb yì ‘wear/put on’ and ‘cover/wrap.’ It cites examples from the Odes for garment/clothing and from Mencius and Han Feizi for wearing. It also lists covering, coating, membrane and moss senses. These attest examples and recorded senses, but do not establish their emergence dates or a linear semantic chain.
evidence.title: 衣 yī、yì - 汉典

evidence.field: File summary; original file link; file history; license
evidence.text: The exact file page identifies the asset as a modern vector rendering of 衣 in Shang oracle-script style and lists ancient-character databases as sources, including Xiaoxuetang. It records a public-domain release for the SVG representation. The asset is a redraw, not an artifact photograph. The exact original image link is https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/f/f4/%E8%A1%A3-oracle.svg.

search_audit.outcome: Han Dian was inspected for lexical senses and cited examples. The Baxter–Sagart PDF could not be inspected in this invocation; local exact rows supplied in the input were checked as local data only.

gaps: The exact oracle-style image is documented on Commons and has an established reusable license, but its original upload.wikimedia.org URL returned a cache-miss error when opened through the browser; it is listed as a candidate because the exact file page links it as the original file. The acquisition system must confirm availability before use.

No separate selected seal-script glyph is offered: the two failed image URLs from the input are excluded, and the inspected alternate Shuowen radical image is a modern redraw with CC BY-SA terms and weaker form-specific provenance.

The earliest dated attestation of 衣 specifically meaning ‘upper garment’ is not established here. CUHK reports early oracle-bone uses mainly as names; its bronze clothing example is not independently dated here. Han Dian lists classic examples, but those do not establish sense origins.
The extension from upper garment to clothing generally, cover, coating, membrane or moss is not traced through dated stages. The graph’s depiction and later lexical uses should be treated separately.
天亡簋 衣祀 remains disputed in the dossier’s cited scholarship; it does not securely establish a ritual sense or whole-graph loan for 衣.
The proposed Proto-Sino-Tibetan comparison and Burmese cognate were not independently verified from an accessible comparative source. No borrowing or sound relationship is asserted.

The provided local Baxter–Sagart rows and local Unihan kMandarin row are not externally verified in this invocation. The prescribed PDF and official Unicode record were not successfully inspected; no verified click-through reading claim is made.
No local bulk extract is recommended: no reuse permission for recurring paleographic database text was verified, and the precise earliest form dating remains unresolved.
